title: Discovery Engine: First-Year SIP Continuity Findings
answer_in_five_lines: **Most of what we collected is general SIP talk. The problem-specific core is small and we analyse it separately:** 32,868 early-journey episodes (first-time investors, or within 12 months of starting), of which **684 are stop stories, 405 are considering stopping, and 1156 kept going**.

**Losses make first-year investors *think* about stopping; mechanics make them *actually* stop.** Among those considering stopping, 55% describe negative returns. Among those who stopped, the most common routes are payment lapse (35%) and app friction (30%); returns disappointment is 21%.

**The two strongest separators between stoppers and continuers are payment/AutoPay problems and 'where is my money' / unresolved support.** Both point the same way on Reddit, YouTube and app reviews (opportunity table, §3).

**It happens early:** 49% of first-time stoppers who say when they stopped did so within 3 months, and 25% at months 7–12. In dated events, months 0–3 mix set-up problems (first-debit problem or failed payment 7%, confused in the app 6%) with early losses (9%); from month 4, seeing losses or flat returns dominates (24%–29%).

**Continuers hold a long-term frame** (71% of their reasons). Almost nobody describes skipping, pausing or reducing *instead of* stopping (reduced instead 1%; skipped or paused instead 0%; n=298). The flexibility exists in apps but is rarely described as the thing that kept someone going.

**Caveat that shapes Part 3.** Public posts over-represent loud failures; people who simply drift away rarely post. The payment/friction story is strongly evidenced; the size of quiet drift is not knowable from public data and is the main thing the interviews must test.

Gate-positive, extracted with H11 deterministic overrides

opportunities.name: Payment & AutoPay problems (early-journey stories)
opportunities.definition: Payment reliability in the first months: failed or missed first debits, AutoPay/mandate set-up and failures, SIP date confusion

opportunities.name: Where is my money / order status + support that resolves
opportunities.definition: Where is my money / order status, and support that resolves (money stuck, units not allotted, tickets closed unresolved)

opportunities.name: Returns vs expectations (loss, flat, "is this normal?")
opportunities.definition: Expectations vs what they see: negative or flat returns, confusing numbers, why negative, is this normal
opportunities.addressable: Partly: explain, don't advise; no fear or urgency

opportunities.name: Cash-flow shocks (crunch, income change)
opportunities.definition: Cash-flow shocks: cash crunch, income change, life events; affordability

opportunities.name: Control of the SIP (skip, pause, edit, cancel)
opportunities.definition: Control of the SIP: skip, pause, edit, cancel - finding it and having it work

cant_tell_us: **Quiet drift**: people who stop thinking about it and let the SIP lapse rarely post. Size unknown.
**Income stability** cells (variable/gig, business) stay below 30 stories.

**Unmet-need themes**: human–AI agreement on the theme list stayed below the 0.6 κ bar (G2 researcher–Claude κ 0.287, G3 κ 0.357; model–researcher κ 0.323; Claude–model κ 0.817). Themes are used as colour, not as evidence.
